Diet is KEY. Really can't stress that enough. I'll tell you my experience and you can take from that what you will. Started about 3 months ago, middle aged and unhappy with the skinny fat thing going on. So I did some research and totally changed my diet. Stopped eating shit, ice cream, soda, fries etc... and focused only on real foods. Generally, if it doesn't have any packaging or advertising, it's better for you. Another way to look at it is to pretty much stick to the perimeter of your grocery store. Produce, meat and some dairy. I also started doing (IF) intermittent fasting (YouTube that shit) and some low impact weight lifting. In that time I've lost about 20lbs, dropped body fat by about 2%,lost 2in on my waist and gained about 3lbs of muscle. A few key take aways: Count them calories. Do it. Obsessively. At least initially. You need to be in a caloric deficit in order to lose weight, so if you're not yet in a deficit then you're not accomplishing anything. Get a scale and use that shit. Weigh yourself every morning in the same circumstances. For example, I get up, piss, then weigh myself in my underwear. Your weight will fluctuate by a couple pounds throughout the course of the day. The idea is to try and get some consistent readings. This was SUPER important for me. Fact is I knew I was making progress even when the mirror wasn't yet showing it. That knowledge was motivating, and let's be honest here, when we're talking about changing behavior that motivation is critical. The other great thing about the scale was that I could tell how different foods effect me. Once I simplified my diet and could reasonably predict to some extent how my weight would change day to day, I started adding other foods. Found out my body doesn't like fries much. However, carbs from beans don't have a negative impact. Not everyone's body handles shit the same so pay attention. IF works. I'm a believer for sure. Look it up and you'll find it's fairly popular in lifting circles. The key to IF success for me was to make sure I was eating real food. I found that if I got my calories from real food during the day, then I wasn't even hungry in the evenings. Wasn't difficult at all. However, if I cheated at lunch and had a bigass burger and fries, even though I had consumed more calories, I was STARVING come dinner time. That's a bit frustrating. Meal prep. Not necessary, but it's been really helpful for me. By making my meals ahead of time it means that not only do I know exactly what's in my food, but I also know what the caloric count is and it saves me a tone of time. This morning I woke up and pulled out a jar of overnight oats from the fridge that I prepared Sunday and walked out the door. The shits delicious and it saves times. I also took one of my lunches I prepared Sunday as I walked out the door. I still have another one waiting in the fridge before I need to cook again. It's been a huge time saver for me. As for exercising, while that's great, I wouldn't necessarily worry too much about it initially. Go for walks in the evening at first. Being fat and out of shape can make even light exercise a grueling slog. Once you've lost some weight, you'll have more energy and you'll be putting less weight on your joints. That's it for now, lemme know if you have questions, and good luck!
